_comment: Town directory. Listings are free and always will be. RULES, kept here so they survive the person who wrote them: (1) An entry goes in only when its details have been checked live — a dead link is worse than a missing entry, same rule as report-it. (2) `checked` is the date that happened; it is printed, so rot is visible rather than silent. (3) Commercial categories — shops, cafés & food, trades, accommodation — are OPEN and grow as businesses ask. Every business in Largs has the same route in and the same terms: free, alphabetical, no ranking, added the same day the details are checked live, competitor or not. No commercial list is ever claimed complete; every open category page says the list is growing and how to get on it, so absence reads as 'not sent in yet', never 'not recommended'. Earlier thinking (Aug 2026) held these categories empty until complete. Dropped 31 Aug 2026: complete is never reachable because shops open and close, and holding back the early askers punishes the people who engaged. Descriptions are the site's own factual words — what they do, when open, where — never the business's own adjectives. (4) No ranking, no ratings, no reviews. Alphabetical within a category, and that is the whole editorial policy. Churches: St Columba's PARISH church (Church of Scotland, Gallowgate Street) is deliberately absent — the congregation united into Cumbrae, Fairlie & Largs and the building was sold, bid accepted February 2026. Do not re-add it from a directory site. The St Columba's that IS listed is the Scottish Episcopal church on Aubery Crescent, a different denomination in a different building. Churches, two traps recorded so they are not walked into again: (1) St Columba's PARISH church (Church of Scotland, Gallowgate Street) is gone — the congregation united into Cumbrae, Fairlie & Largs and the building was sold, bid accepted February 2026. The St Columba's that IS listed is the Scottish Episcopal church on Aubery Crescent: different denomination, different building. (2) Clark Memorial Church and Largs Community Church are THE SAME BUILDING on Bath Street. CFL's own site calls it Largs Parish Church; the town and the listed-building record call it Clark Memorial. Both names are in the entry so either search finds it. No service time is stated: CFL lists three times across three sites without saying which is which, and a wrong time sends someone to a locked door. Within a category, entries carry the same KINDS of detail. One entry with a phone number among five without reads as singled out, and the eye treats the difference as meaningful when it is not. If one gets a number, they all do, or none do. Open categories carry their own `asks` list — what to send us differs by trade. Trades must ask for AREA COVERED, never an address: sole traders work from home and a directory should not publish that. Social links: a public Facebook PAGE is fine, a Facebook GROUP is not — a group asks for a login before showing anything, and the readers least likely to have an account are the ones this site is for. Douglas Park BC has only a group, so it carries no link. Largs has THREE bowling clubs and they are distinct: Largs Bowling Club and Douglas Park outdoors, Halkshill indoor and outdoor. Checked 29 Aug 2026 against separate club listings. Fairlie BC uses the Largs Sport Hub but is a Fairlie club and stays out. Descriptions should tell a reader whether the place is FOR THEM — when it opens, whether newcomers are welcome, what happens there that a non-member might care about. St Columba's Episcopal is the model: service times, plus a labyrinth anyone can walk and four car boot sales a year. A line that only names the thing is a label, not an entry. `checked` is RECORDED BUT NOT PRINTED. It is maintenance metadata: it tells the maintainer when an entry was last verified and would drive a 'nothing checked in a year' review. It was on the page and came off on 29 Aug 2026 — a date only says the entry was right on that one day, which does not help a reader decide anything, and it was a fourth line on every entry. Honest badging is for data whose FRESHNESS CHANGES THE ANSWER — tides, fuel, roadworks. A church's address is not that. The corrections route and the 'who have we missed' line are the honesty mechanism here. If it ever goes back on the page, write it as 'August 2026', not an ISO date. Logo spec, published on the open categories: square, the MARK ONLY not a wordmark version, 256px or larger, and we crop. The mark-only part is the one that matters — a file with the name in it renders the name twice and leaves the symbol at half size. Verified by looking on 29 Aug 2026. Third-party logos: a badge is used because a directory listing carrying an organisation's own mark is ordinary practice and helps them. But they were not asked first, so every category page carries a plain opt-out line. If anyone asks, it comes off the same day, no argument. Rejected on 29 Aug: Routenburn (103px, and the image found may not even be their badge — never publish a mark you are not sure belongs to the name) and sportscotland Inverclyde (a pure wordmark, which at 56px is an unreadable blue square). LOGO ATTRIBUTION: the mark must belong to the thing named in the entry, not to its landlord, operator or governing body. Largs Inspire Badminton, Largs Colts and Largs TAGB all meet at a KA Leisure venue; putting KA Leisure's mark on them would say KA Leisure runs three clubs it does not. An operator's mark is fair only where the ENTRY is that operator's own — Vikingar! and Barrfields Theatre — and even then the venue's own branding comes first. CRESTS READ AS TEXTURE, NOT DETAIL. A club crest with banners — Largs Colts has two, plus thistles, a longship and a horse — reduces to a smudge at 56px. Taken anyway: it still reads as 'a football badge', clubs like seeing their badge shown, and excluding them would exclude exactly the local institutions whose marks mean most to residents. Judge new ones by rendering at 56px first, not at full size. NO LOGOS ON CHURCHES — decided 29 Aug 2026, and it is a deliberate absence, not a gap waiting to be filled. What is available is DENOMINATIONAL emblems (United Free, Church of Scotland, Episcopal, Catholic), not the individual congregations' own marks. Carrying them would put this site in the position of representing each tradition's identity, which is the congregations' job and not a town directory's, and any unevenness in how they rendered would read as a slight nobody intended. Adding one and not the others is worse again. If a single congregation ever asks for its own mark to be shown, that is a different question and worth reconsidering — but not one taken on the site's own initiative. CLUBS vs COMMUNITY GROUPS: a club exists for its MEMBERS — bowling, badminton, table tennis. A community group exists for the TOWN or the PLACE — looking after a shared space, a friends-of group, a development trust, a food bank. Something that does both, like Rotary, goes under community groups, because the point of it is what it does for others. Cairnie's Quay is a mooring association and could sit under Sailing & marina; it is here because its own description leads with looking after a shared space, the environment and the people who use it. SOCIAL LINKS are a second, optional link — `social: {label, url}` — for groups whose Facebook page is where things actually happen. The MAIN url must always be one that works without a login; a Facebook group behind a login is never the primary link. Label it plainly so nobody is surprised by a login wall. Amber Counselling & Yoga was held back on 29 Aug pending permission to publish the logo, and restored on 30 Aug once given. That is the rule: a business's own mark goes up when they have said yes, not before.

categories.label: Clubs & societies
categories.blurb: Groups that meet in Largs and welcome new members.

entries.name: Douglas Park Bowling Club
entries.blurb: Around a hundred members and known locally as the friendly club. As much a social club as a bowling one — bridge, quiz nights and rainbow whist run alongside the green, and new members are welcome.

entries.name: Largs Bowling Club
entries.blurb: Lawn bowls on Douglas Street, green open seven days. New members of any age or ability are welcome and coaching is free, so no experience needed to turn up.

entries.name: Largs Colts
entries.blurb: Youth football, training and playing at the Community Sport Hub on Alexander Avenue.

entries.name: Largs Halkshill Bowling Club
entries.blurb: Bowls indoors and out — the only Largs club with both. The green was laid in 1888 with turf from the Halkshill estate, which is where the name comes from. The clubhouse takes bookings for functions.

entries.name: Largs Inspire Badminton Club
entries.blurb: Badminton for children aged 5 to 13, at the Community Sport Hub on Alexander Avenue.

entries.name: Largs TAGB
entries.blurb: Taekwondo at the Community Sport Hub, under the Tang Soo Do Association of Great Britain.

entries.name: Largs Table Tennis Club
entries.blurb: Table tennis on Brisbane Road, for complete beginners as well as players who want a competitive game.

categories.label: Community groups
categories.blurb: Volunteer groups working for the town, the coast and the people in it.

entries.name: Cairnie's Quay Mooring Association
entries.blurb: A volunteer-run association looking after Cairnie's Quay — the slipway, the quay itself and 28 moorings. As well as boat owners it supports wild swimmers, divers, paddleboarders and anglers, and runs beach clean-ups and social meet-ups.

categories.label: Shops
categories.blurb: Shops and high-street services in Largs.

entries.name: Gallery Eight Picture Framing
entries.blurb: Picture framing done on the premises — originals, prints, photographs, certificates, tapestries and sports strips among the things they have framed. Formerly Largs DIY: the hardware side has gone and the framing continues. Open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday, 10am–2pm.
entries.note: They close at short notice now and again — worth a call before a special trip.

entries.name: LPC Design + Print
entries.blurb: Graphic design, websites and printing — business cards, leaflets, wedding stationery, books and magazines — plus printing on t-shirts, hoodies and bags with no minimum order. The copy shop counter is open Monday to Friday, 10am–12.30pm and 1.30pm–4pm; for design and print work it is worth phoning ahead. On Main Street since 1970, in the old production plant of the Largs and Millport Weekly News.

entries.name: Studio 44 Gallery
entries.blurb: Art gallery showing changing exhibitions of original work by contemporary Scottish artists — paintings, ceramics, jewellery, photography — for sale. Open 11am–5pm, Tuesday to Saturday, while an exhibition is on. The space can also be hired for art classes, workshops, meetings and pop-up events: evenings from 6pm, and all day Sunday and Monday during exhibitions.

categories.label: Health & wellbeing
categories.blurb: Counselling, therapies, classes and practitioners in Largs.

entries.name: Amber Counselling & Yoga
entries.blurb: Counselling and yoga in Largs and online. Laura Hendry is an integrative counsellor and psychotherapist registered with BACP and COSCA, and the first consultation is free. Yoga runs as group and one-to-one classes — Hatha, flow, yin and restorative — with parent and teen sessions too.

categories.label: Halls for hire
categories.blurb: Rooms and halls in Largs available to book.

entries.name: Barrfields Theatre
entries.blurb: A 470-seat theatre at Vikingar!, available for hire through KA Leisure.

entries.name: Largs Community Sport Hub
entries.blurb: Two halls, seating around 250 and 350, bookable through KA Leisure.

entries.name: Largs Parish Church halls
entries.blurb: Halls and meeting spaces at the Bath Street church, with availability published online.

entries.name: Brisbane Evangelical Church
entries.blurb: An independent evangelical congregation on School Street, answering to no wider denomination.

entries.name: Largs Parish Church (Clark Memorial)
entries.blurb: Church of Scotland, part of the Cumbrae, Fairlie and Largs parish. The 1892 building on Bath Street is category A listed and holds a Grade 1 listed Father Willis organ, one of the finest of his instruments in Scotland. Sunday morning worship — see their site for the current time.

entries.name: Largs United Free Church
entries.blurb: United Free Church of Scotland, on Brisbane Road near the fire station. A small congregation from the tradition that stayed out of the 1929 union.

entries.name: St Columba's Scottish Episcopal Church
entries.blurb: Scottish Episcopal, at the corner of Aubery Crescent and Greenock Road, with 19th-century connections to Lord Kelvin. Communion at 8am and Eucharist at 11am on Sundays, Communion at 10am on Wednesdays. The Largs Labyrinth is on the north lawn behind the church, open to anyone who wants to walk it, and the congregation runs car boot sales on the grounds four times a year — pitches go early.

entries.name: St Mary's Star of the Sea
entries.blurb: Roman Catholic, sharing a parish with Millport. The Greenock Road church is unmistakable from the front: a steep timber-clad gable with a granite statue of Our Lady beside it.

categories.label: Sport & leisure
categories.blurb: Places to swim, play, train and watch sport in Largs.

entries.name: Largs Golf Club
entries.blurb: An 18-hole parkland course south of the town, established in 1891, with views over the Clyde to Cumbrae, Bute and Arran. Visitors welcome and tee times bookable online.

entries.name: Largs Thistle F.C.
entries.blurb: Founded in 1889 and playing in the West of Scotland League Premier Division, at Barrfields Park.

entries.name: Routenburn Golf Club
entries.blurb: A short course above the town, par 68, with panoramic views over the Firth of Clyde to Arran and the Cumbraes. A small, friendly club — sloping greens, blind tee shots and fees they reckon are the cheapest for miles. Visitors welcome, and there's a bar and a pro shop on site.

entries.name: sportscotland National Centre Inverclyde
entries.blurb: A residential sports training centre in 86 acres above the town, taking group bookings for facilities and organised activities.
entries.note: The golf training centre here closed permanently on 31 March 2026.

entries.name: Vikingar!
entries.blurb: A four-lane 25m pool and teaching pool, gym, the Viking Experience, Multiball and a café, alongside Barrfields Theatre. Run by KA Leisure.

categories.label: Sailing & marina
categories.blurb: Berthing, boatyards and sailing on the Largs Channel.

entries.name: Largs Sailing Club
entries.blurb: At the Yacht Haven. Dinghy racing, RYA training through the LSTA, and an active cruising section for sail and power. The Lookout Lounge has an honesty café open daily.

entries.name: Largs Yacht Haven
entries.blurb: Marina berthing, lifting and launching, dry berthing and a boatyard, on the shore south of the town.
